question.html:
A monatomic ideal gas is trapped in a cylinder by a piston. The following data are available.

Initial pressure of gas

= 1.00 × 105 Pa

Initial temperature

= 712 K

Quantity of gas

= 6.00 × 10−4 mol

The gas undergoes an adiabatic expansion to a volume of 8.00 × 10−5 m3.

a.i Determine the pressure of the gas after the adiabatic expansion. [3]

a.ii Determine the work done by the gas during the expansion. [3]

b The gas then undergoes an isobaric compression until its volume is equal to the initial volume.

b.i Calculate the energy removed in this isobaric compression. [3]

b.ii The gas returns to its original state in an isovolumetric change. The energy supplied during this change is 3.9 J. Calculate the efficiency of this cycle. [1]

b.iii Outline why it is important that engines are designed with high efficiency even though all engines obey the first law of thermodynamics. [1]
